newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore share index down ahead of bonus revision.
newsitem.headline: Singapore share index down ahead of bonus revision.

text.p: The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) skidded lower early on Thursday on a continuation of institutional selling and ahead of a bonus adjustment.
The benchmark STII collapsed in early action spurred by fund selling of banks and property shares, but the extent of the fall was exaggerated by Keppel Corp's bonus issue, dealers said.
"It looks so bad because the index is reflecting the ex-bonus (price) for Keppel," a local brokerage dealer said.
At 0215 GMT, the STII was assessed at 2,000.79, down 34.01 points. Dealers said this should be about 15 points higher when the stock exchange makes an adjustment for Keppel Corp.
The shipping conglomerate proposed a one-for-four bonus issue last month despite reporting a 4.7 percent drop in net profit to $204.10 million for the year ended December 31, 1996.
Dealers said market sentiment was still bearish with more price falls expected as foreign funds continued to shift out of poorly performing regional markets.
Blue chips lost more ground, with Cycle & Carriage easing Singapore 30 cents to $14.50 and SPH foreign down 30 cents to S$27.10. Keppel was down S$1.80 to S$6.85 on its bonus split.
SIA foreign was among top gainers, up 10 cents to S$12.50.
